hero.title: Pallava and Chalukyan Architecture
hero.description: An analytical study of the evolutionary transition from rock-cut shrines to structural temples in Peninsular India.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Tracing the shift from Mahendra-style rock-cut caves to the climax of the Dravidian architectural tradition.

cards.details: Mahendravarman I initiates the Pallava rock-cut cave temple tradition in Tamil Nadu.
Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla) introduces the monolithic Rathas at Mahabalipuram.
Rajasimha phase; transition to structural temples (Kailasanatha at Kanchipuram, Shore Temple).

items.title: M.M.R.S (Pallava Style)
items.decryption: Chronological stages: Mahendra (Pillar/Cave), Mamalla (Monoliths), Rajasimha (Structural), Nandivarman (Final structural refinement).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing rock-cut caves with monolithic rathas; remember, rathas are carved out of single boulders, not caves.
Thinking all Dravidian temples are solely Pallava creations; acknowledge the Chalukyan influence of the Vesara style.
Assuming the Shore Temple is rock-cut; it is a landmark structural temple built by Rajasimha.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Pallavas: Kanchipuram, Mahabalipuram
  • Chalukyas: Badami, Aihole, Pattadakal

Personalities

  • Mahendravarman I: Founder of cave style
  • Pulakeshin II: Patron of Badami caves
  • Narasimhavarman I: Mamallapuram sculptor

Architectural Evolution Mindmap

  • Pallava Phase
    • Mahendra Style: Pillar-based cave temples.
    • Mamalla Style: Monolithic Rathas (Five Rathas).
    • Rajasimha Style: Structural temples (Kailasanatha).
  • Chalukyan Phase
    • Badami Caves: Synthesis of Nagara and Dravida elements.
    • Aihole: "Cradle of Temple Architecture" (Lad Khan temple).
    • Pattadakal: UNESCO site, blend of North and South styles.
